memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After Moses finished writing in a book the words of this law from beginning to end, he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord: 'Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God. There it will remain as a witness against you.'" — Deut 31:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses finished writing the entire law "from beginning to end," and commanded that the book be placed beside the ark of the covenant — the most sacred spot in Israel, at the very centre of their worship. There the Word of God would remain "as a witness." God's law was not to be hidden away and forgotten, but kept in the holiest place, permanently testifying to God's truth and to His people's accountability before Him.

There is something profound in placing the Word beside the ark. The ark represented God's presence and, inside it, the mercy seat where atonement was made. And right beside it stood the law. Together they tell the whole story: God's holy standard, and God's provision of mercy. We need both. The law shows us God's righteousness and our shortfall; the mercy seat shows us God's grace.

The law standing "as a witness" reminds us that God's Word measures our lives truthfully. It does not flatter us; it tells us the truth about ourselves. That can be uncomfortable, but it is a mercy, for only truth can lead us to genuine repentance and grace.

Wonderfully, the whole arrangement points to Christ. He is both the fulfilment of the law and our mercy seat, the "atoning sacrifice for our sins" (1 John 2:2). Where the law witnesses against us, Jesus stands as our advocate, having satisfied its every demand. So we need not fear the witness of the Word. In Christ, the law's verdict is answered, and mercy has the final say.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I let God's Word tell me the truth about myself, even when uncomfortable?
2. How do the law and God's mercy work together in my understanding?
3. How does Christ change the way I hear the "witness" of Scripture?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your Word tells me the truth and leads me to grace. Where the law witnesses against me, thank You that Christ is my mercy and my advocate. Let mercy have the final word in me. Amen.
